decisionsTitle: The calendar entry asks Da / Nu / Poate, and the answers go where the club says (amending §107, §174)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-08:** «On the iCal calendar, can we make it Smarter so that people can respond Going/NotGoing and replying to [the club's Gmail]?» Then, on bloat: «Will this bloat up the app? Can this be a config? In Gmail I can setup a filter I guess». The address he named is the club's Gmail; the repository is public, so it is written nowhere here, and it is typed in the app.

**What he chose.** The answers go to the club's Gmail, an address configured in the app, never in code. No new form and no new data: the invitation rides on the emails a runner already receives — a race's confirmation and reminder, and for a group run the email of the optional declaration they signed (§393, §523). Nothing on the site reads the answers: he reads Gmail, sorted by a filter.

**One setting, not a feature.** «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Răspunsurile din calendar», beside «Copiile clubului» (what else the club receives): one box, «Răspunsurile din calendar merg la» (`platform_settings.calendarRsvpTo`), one address or empty. Trimmed and checked with the platform's email rule (`z.email`), Administrator-only and asserted on the server, asked before saving (§384), audited (`calendar_rsvp_to.changed`, the address before and after, its own entity id `…e0ca`, §483), read by the send through a half-minute memo the save drops. Every reader of the page sees it: it is the club's address, nobody's data. Help under the box, both languages: «Cu o adresă aici, invitația din calendar are Da / Nu / Poate; răspunsurile ajung pe ea. Pont: adresa clubului cu +calendar și un filtru în Gmail.» **Empty — the default, and every deployment until somebody types one — is exactly today**: the confirmation and the reminder carry the `.ics` with `METHOD:PUBLISH`, no organizer and no attendee, and no other message carries one; a test pins that file byte for byte against what the code before this wrote. Never a default address in code.

**The invitation** (`events/ical.ts`, `buildCalendar` and `buildVEvent` with `rsvp`). `METHOD:REQUEST`; `ORGANIZER;CN=<the club's name>:mailto:<the setting>`; `ATTENDEE;CN=<name>;ROLE=REQ-PARTICIPANT;PARTSTAT=NEEDS-ACTION;RSVP=TRUE:mailto:<the address the message goes to>` — the address the calendar app matches against its own account to offer the answer; `SEQUENCE:<n>`; `STATUS:CONFIRMED`; `DTSTAMP` the moment the message is made (RFC 5546 §2.1.5), `LAST-MODIFIED` the entry's own stamp (§159). The same `UID` as the public feed's entry, `<event id>@<this deployment's host>` (§107, §174 — QA's and production's never merge), so an invitation and a subscribed feed are one event in the app, not two. **One VEVENT**: the programme rows the feed writes as entries of their own (§117) are in the description only — every further VEVENT would be another invitation to answer. A cancellation is `METHOD:CANCEL` with `STATUS:CANCELLED` and an attendee line that asks nothing. Escaped and folded as every line (75 octets, never a split character); a typed name with a comma, a colon or a semicolon is quoted, and a double quote or a line break in it cannot break the line. No calendar name and no refresh hint — a feed's lines, not an invitation's. The QA mark on the title, as before. The attendee's name is a minor's parent or guardian's (§108), else the person's (a family's one confirmation greets the person of its first form, §519), the signer's typed name on a group run.

**Where it goes while the setting is set** — one table, `notifications/domain/calendar-part.ts` (`calendarPartFor`): the confirmation and the reminder carry the invitation instead of the file; the group run's signed declaration carries it to the signer, for the date signed on (a series' declaration covers every date, §523; the invitation is that date's entry, as the feed's is); «Detalii actualizate» carries the updated invitation when its kinds include the time, the place or a date on again (`changesTheCalendar`) — never for the programme or a note alone; the cancellation carries `CANCEL`. **Only to a person who holds a place**: the update and the cancellation also reach the waiting list and the pending declarations (§331), and «Vii?» to somebody without a place would be wrong; a confirmation rendered for a registration no longer confirmed keeps the file. Never on a club copy or an archive copy (§320: the rule is no attachment). Published, dated events only, as since §174 and §533. A family's one confirmation is one invitation, to the address. The method follows the event as it stands at the send (§331): a request rendered after the date was cancelled goes as its cancellation — never a «Vii?» for a race called off — and a cancellation rendered after the date is on again carries nothing, since the notice saying so carries the invitation.

**SEQUENCE is a column, `events.calendar_sequence`** (migration `0132`, expand only, default 0), bumped in the save's own transaction for every date whose start, race start or shown place moved, that was cancelled, or that is on again — the comparison «Detalii actualizate» already makes (`calendarSequenceMoves` over `eventChangesToAnnounce`), made on every save **whether or not the organizer tells anybody**; a series save bumps every date it moved, and reads the other dates back only when this one moved. Why: a calendar keeps the highest `SEQUENCE` it has read for a UID and ignores a lower one, so the number must rise whenever what the entry says about when, where and whether changes — also when nobody was told, because the next reminder or confirmation carries the new time and must outrank the copy the runner's calendar holds. Counting the audited changes was refused: the audit has a row only when the organizer told, and it would be a query per message. `version` was refused: every save and every supplementary place moves it, and Outlook and Google treat a raised `SEQUENCE` as a significant update that may ask an answered invitation again — over a typo. A programme row, the end or a note moves nothing (an equal `SEQUENCE` with a later `DTSTAMP` is still read as the newer copy, RFC 5546 §2.1.5). The cancellation's `CANCEL` carries the bumped number, so it outranks the last `REQUEST`; a date on again bumps once more, so its next `REQUEST` outranks the `CANCEL`.

**The MIME, and what was verified.** A calendar app offers the answer buttons for a part typed `text/calendar; method=REQUEST`. Nodemailer's `icalEvent` (already installed: the Gmail road's library) composes the shape Google Calendar's own invitations have — `multipart/mixed` { `multipart/alternative` { the text, the HTML, `text/calendar; charset=utf-8; method=REQUEST` }, the other attachments (the signed declaration beside a confirmation, §174), `application/ics; name=invite.ics` }. The Gmail road hands `icalEvent` to `sendMail`. Mailgun's form API (`text`, `html`, `attachment`, `inline`) has no alternative part, and its users report that an attached `.ics` leaves without the `method` parameter — Gmail reads the file's own `METHOD:` and copes, Outlook does not. So the Mailgun road composes the same message with Nodemailer's `MailComposer` and posts it whole to `messages.mime` (Mailgun's reference, «Send an email in MIME format»: `to` carrying every envelope recipient, `message` as a file, the same `o:`, `h:` and `v:` options): tracking off, the outbox key, the locale and environment tags as on every message; a message without an invitation goes to `messages` exactly as before. One rendering (`render.ts` builds the `.ics` once, `OutgoingEmail.calendar = { method, ics }`), one composer, two roads. Verified by the tests: the composed bytes (the part's content type with the method, the `invite.ics` attachment, From, To, Cc and Reply-To, no Bcc header, the envelope), the Mailgun endpoint and form fields, Gmail's `icalEvent`. Not verified here: a live Gmail, Outlook or Apple inbox drawing the buttons, and Mailgun's acceptance of a `messages.mime` post from this account (its documentation could not be fetched from the build machine; the endpoint and fields are from its reference as published) — the first real send on QA is that check.

**What a reply is.** The runner's calendar app sends «Accepted: <event> …» (or declined, or tentative) to the organizer's address. Nothing on the site reads it. `SETUP.md` §38 step 8 says how: the setting on each deployment, the club's Gmail with `+calendar` before the `@`, and a Gmail filter — **To** the `+calendar` address → label «Calendar», skip the inbox.

**What does not change.** The public feed and the event page's `.ics` stay `METHOD:PUBLISH`, byte for byte: a subscriber is asked nothing. Google's add-event link is unchanged. No new data about a person is stored, and the emails' words are unchanged.

**The privacy notice: no sentence.** The invitation names the person's own address to the person. The answer is their own act, sent by their calendar to a club address shown in the invitation, as a reply to an email is; the club's mailbox is already named (section 6). Nothing the platform keeps changes. If the club ever counts or keeps the answers anywhere but its mailbox, that is a new purpose, and the notice says so first.

**Refused.**
- A «Vin» form on the group-run pages: a public form, a list of addresses kept per run and a notice change — the owner chose the declaration's email.
- Reading the answers on the site (an inbound address, a parser, a list on the event): the owner reads Gmail, and a filter sorts it.
- `version`, or a count of audit rows, as `SEQUENCE` (above).
- One VEVENT per programme row in an invitation: each would be one more invitation to answer.
- Mailgun's attachment alone, typed `method=REQUEST`: reported not to keep the parameter, which Outlook needs.
- The invitation on any other message, or a `CANCEL` when a person cancels their own registration: not asked (a question to the owner).

**Consequences.** `events/ical.ts` (`CalendarRsvp`, `rsvp` on `buildVEvent` and `buildCalendar`), `events/domain/event-changes.ts` (`CALENDAR_CHANGE_KINDS`, `changesTheCalendar`, `calendarSequenceMoves`), `content/events/service.ts` (`bumpCalendarSequences` in both saves), `db/schema/events.ts` + migration `0132_calendar_sequence`, `events/repository.ts` (the sequence with the email's event rows), `notifications/calendar-rsvp.ts` + `domain/calendar-rsvp.ts` (the setting, its memo), `notifications/calendar-part.ts` + `domain/calendar-part.ts`, `notifications/render.ts`, `notifications/templates.ts`, `infrastructure/email/adapter.ts` (`calendar`), `calendar-mime.ts`, `mailgun-adapter.ts`, `gmail-adapter.ts`, `ui/CalendarRsvpPanel.tsx`, the «Emailuri» page and its action, the catalogues, `SETUP.md` §38 step 8. Tests: unit `events/ical-invitation.test.ts`, `notifications/calendar-invitation-mime.test.ts`, `notifications/calendar-part.test.ts`; integration `notifications/calendar-invitation.test.ts`; e2e `email-plan.spec.ts` (the panel, read-only and saved).
changelogLine: - **The calendar entry can ask «Da / Nu / Poate»** — with one address in «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Răspunsurile din calendar», the confirmation, the reminder, a group run's signed declaration, a time or place update and a cancellation carry an invitation the runner's calendar answers, and the answers land in that mailbox; empty, the calendar file is exactly as before. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given «Răspunsurile din calendar merg la» set, when a message carries the event as an invitation, then the file is `METHOD:REQUEST` (`CANCEL` for a cancellation) with one VEVENT — the public feed's `UID`, `SEQUENCE` from `events.calendar_sequence`, `STATUS:CONFIRMED` (`CANCELLED`), `DTSTAMP` the message's moment, `ORGANIZER;CN=<the club>:mailto:<the setting>` and one `ATTENDEE` for the address the message goes to with `PARTSTAT=NEEDS-ACTION;RSVP=TRUE` (asking nothing on a cancellation) — the programme in the description and never as entries of its own, every line escaped and folded, a typed name quoted when it must be, no calendar name and no refresh hint; `calendar_sequence` rises with every save that moves a date's start, race start or shown place, cancels it or puts it on again — told or not, every date a series save moves included — and with nothing else; without the setting, the feed, the page's file and the emails' file are unchanged byte for byte (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `events/ical-invitation.test.ts`, `notifications/calendar-part.test.ts`; integration `notifications/calendar-invitation.test.ts`.

Given «Răspunsurile din calendar merg la» empty (the default), then criterion 11 holds unchanged and no other message carries a calendar part; given an address, then the confirmation and the reminder carry the invitation instead of the file, a group run's signed declaration carries it to the signer, «Detalii actualizate» carries it when its changes include the time, the place or a date on again, and the cancellation carries its cancellation — the method as the event stands at the send (a request for a date cancelled since goes as its cancellation, a cancellation for a date on again carries nothing), only to a person who holds a place, never on a club copy or an archive copy, for a published, dated event only; on both roads the part leaves as a `text/calendar; charset=utf-8; method=REQUEST` (or `CANCEL`) alternative and an `invite.ics` attachment — Gmail through Nodemailer's `icalEvent`, Mailgun as the same message composed whole and posted to `messages.mime` with tracking off, the outbox key and the tags — and a message without one is posted to `messages` as before (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `notifications/calendar-invitation-mime.test.ts`, `notifications/calendar-part.test.ts`; integration `notifications/calendar-invitation.test.ts`.

Given «Setări» → «Emailuri», then «Răspunsurile din calendar» sits beside «Copiile clubului»: a closed fold with its glyph whose summary names the address or says it is off, the address in force named above one box «Răspunsurile din calendar merg la» with its help in both languages; every reader of the page sees it and only an Administrator saves it — asserted on the server, asked first (§384) — an entry that is not one address is refused naming the box with what was typed kept, the value is trimmed, empty is off, and every save writes `calendar_rsvp_to.changed` with the address before and after (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: integration `notifications/calendar-invitation.test.ts`, e2e `email-plan.spec.ts`.

batchLine: the calendar entry in the confirmation, the reminder, a group run's declaration, a time or place update and a cancellation asks «Da / Nu / Poate» once the club names, in «Emailuri», the address the answers go to; empty, the file is as before
